record.context_brief: Ergodic compact-group actions on Neumann algebras
record.original_question: Let G be a compact group, let M be a Neumann algebra, and let σ: G → Aut(M) be an ergodic action of G on M. Is M necessarily finite?

evidence.quote: Let an action σ: G→Aut(M) of the compact group G on the Neumann algebra M be ergodic. Is M necessarily finite?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a compact (Hausdorff topological) group and let $M$ be a von Neumann algebra. Suppose $\sigma\colon G\to \mathrm{Aut}(M)$ is an action of $G$ on $M$ by $*$-automorphisms which is ergodic, in the sense that the fixed-point algebra
$$M^{\sigma}=\{x\in M : \sigma_g(x)=x \text{ for all } g\in G\}$$
equals $\mathbb{C}\,1$. (Continuity of $g\mapsto \sigma_g(x)$ in the appropriate topology is assumed, e.g.\ $\sigma$ is pointwise $\sigma$-weakly continuous.)

Must $M$ be a finite von Neumann algebra, i.e.\ must $M$ admit a faithful normal tracial state (equivalently, must the unique $G$-invariant normal state on $M$ be a trace)?
artifact.category_tag: Operator algebras / ergodic actions on von Neumann algebras
artifact.status_search_result: The question was answered affirmatively by Høegh-Krohn, Landstad and Størmer: if a compact group acts ergodically on a unital C*-algebra (in particular on a von Neumann algebra), the unique invariant state is a trace, so the von Neumann algebra is finite (and in fact injective). This is a classical, well-cited finiteness theorem, with later extensions to compact quantum groups.

status_evidence.title: Ergodic actions of compact groups on operator algebras (Høegh-Krohn, Landstad, Størmer)
status_evidence.snippet: If G is a compact ergodic group of *-automorphisms of a unital C*-algebra A, then the unique G-invariant state is a trace; hence if A is a von Neumann algebra it is finite.
status_evidence.claim: The original Høegh-Krohn–Landstad–Størmer theorem proves the von Neumann algebra must be finite under an ergodic compact-group action.

status_evidence.title: Growth rates of dimensional invariants of compact quantum groups and a theorem of Høegh-Krohn, Landstad and Størmer
status_evidence.snippet: For compact groups, this reduces to the finiteness theorem of Hoegh-Krohn, Landstad and Stormer.
status_evidence.claim: The classical compact-group case is referred to as a finiteness theorem, confirming the question is settled affirmatively.
